prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and approach
- “Forward, Together”: strong and stable leadership to deliver Brexit and tackle five challenges—economic strength, Brexit/changing world, social divisions, ageing society, and fast-changing technology.
- Govern from the mainstream; use the state as a force for good; focus on ordinary working families; pragmatic, evidence-led Conservatism.

Economy and industrial strategy
- Balance the budget by the mid-2020s; low taxes (no VAT rise; personal allowance to £12,500 and higher rate to £50,000 by 2020; corporation tax to 17%); simplify taxes and reform business rates.
- Expand trade: “deep and special” EU partnership and new global deals; reinforce UK Export Finance and trade commissioners.
- Update market rules: raise National Living Wage to 60% of median by 2020 then track earnings; protect gig economy workers; crack down on tax evasion; tighten pension and takeover rules; curb excessive executive pay and strengthen worker voice on boards.
- Modern Industrial Strategy: raise R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years; £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund for housing, infrastructure, skills and digital; support SMEs (prompt payment, procurement target); energy cost review, diverse energy mix (offshore wind, shale with safeguards), smart meters and an energy efficiency scheme.
- Major infrastructure: HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion; EV ambition (near-zero-emission cars/vans by 2050).

Union, Brexit and global role
- Strengthen the UK union; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum now; create a UK Shared Prosperity Fund (post‑EU funds).
- Brexit: leave single market and customs union; Great Repeal Bill; continuity of EU-derived rights at exit; frictionless Irish border; “no deal better than a bad deal.”
- Global Britain: retain 0.7% aid with tighter rules; meet NATO 2% and grow defence spending; maintain Trident; invest £178bn in equipment; veteran support.

Security, justice and governance
- New national infrastructure police; fold SFO into NCA; bolster counter-terror and cyber.
- Electoral reforms: voter ID, continue boundary review, repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; keep FPTP and extend to PCC/mayors.

Meritocracy, education and skills
- Expand good school places: continue free schools; allow new selective schools with conditions; require universities/independent schools to sponsor state schools; specialist maths schools; admissions review (no lotteries).
- Knowledge-rich curriculum; EBacc expansion; teacher support; fairer funding (+£4bn by 2022); replace universal infant lunches with universal primary breakfasts.
- World-class technical route: T‑levels, institutes of technology, 3m apprenticeships, discounted travel; lifelong learning and a national retraining scheme.

Society, welfare and migration
- Cut net migration to the tens of thousands; tougher rules for non‑EU/family/student visas; integration strategy; Commission for Countering Extremism.
- Close gender and race gaps (pay transparency, stop-and-search reform); new Mental Health Act and 10,000 more staff; disability employment up by 1m; Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; halve rough sleeping this parliament and end by 2027.

NHS, social care and pensions
- NHS: at least £8bn extra over five years; more staff; major buildings/tech upgrade; recoup overseas costs; seven‑day services; retain A&E and 18‑week standards; strengthen mental health, cancer, learning disability and end‑of‑life care.
- Social care: include home value in means test for domiciliary care; £100k asset floor; defer payments until after death; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; maintain bus passes, TV licences, etc.
- Pensions: Triple Lock to 2020, then Double Lock; raise state pension age with longevity; extend auto‑enrolment and support long-term saving.

Housing, communities and environment
- Build 1.5m homes by 2022; quality, density, protect Green Belt; council housing deals with fixed terms and Right to Buy after 10–15 years; reform CPOs; renter protections and leasehold reform.
- Devolution, culture and rural/coastal support; animal welfare (CCTV in abattoirs); 25‑year environment plan; air quality and tree planting.

Digital
- Digital Charter: best place to start/run a digital business and safest online.
- New data protection law; right to delete data at 18; Data Use and Ethics Commission; stronger platform duties on harmful content.
- Full‑fibre and 5G rollout; Verify digital identity; £1.9bn cyber strategy.
